brief.legacy_full_text:
# Approved Design System Brief

## Administrative
- Project: WeGroween
- Client: WeGroween
- Design Decision Leader: User
- Additional approvers: None identified
- Delegated decision scope: Routine implementation and objective quality corrections
- Mode: REFRESH
- Version: 1.0
- Date: 2026-10-02
- Status: approved

## Product understanding
- Product: Premium farm-and-food commerce brand
- Maturity: Existing static catalogue informing a refreshed, implementation-ready design system
- Core offer: Microgreens, mushrooms, organic vegetables and fruits, and exotic farming-related products
- Value proposition: Premium fresh products cultivated and selected with care, authenticity, and credible farm knowledge
- Business model: Household e-commerce with restaurant supply also available

## Users
- Primary audience: Quality-conscious households and home cooks
- Secondary audience: Restaurants, chefs, caterers, and hospitality buyers
- Jobs to be done: Discover trustworthy specialty produce, understand quality and provenance, order conveniently, and manage repeat purchasing
- Trust and accessibility considerations: Freshness, provenance, cultivation practices, delivery clarity, price transparency, readable content, keyboard operation, reduced motion, and WCAG 2.2 AA contrast

## Future product context
- Archetype: E-commerce storefront plus authenticated operations dashboard; implementation is outside the current scope
- Primary conversion: Complete an online purchase
- Secondary conversions: Restaurant-supply enquiry/account onboarding, repeat ordering, WhatsApp support, and product discovery
- Required customer surfaces: Homepage, catalogue, category and search, product detail, cart, checkout, account, order history, restaurant supply, about/provenance, support, and policies
- Required admin surfaces: Sign-in, overview, orders, order detail, products, categories, inventory, customers, restaurant enquiries/accounts, promotions, delivery settings, and basic reporting
- Content status: Existing mushroom and microgreen content is a starting point; organic produce, fruit, exotic-product, provenance, and restaurant content are draft or unavailable

## Brand intent
- Brand-name idea: WeGroween combines “we grow green”
- Desired attributes: Premium, authentic, cultivated, fresh, knowledgeable, warm, trustworthy
- Anti-attributes: Generic eco branding, bargain-market styling, artificial luxury, clinical sterility, decorative green clichés, and unsubstantiated wellness claims
- Emotional objective: Quiet confidence in unusually fresh, carefully grown food
- Tone: Knowledgeable, transparent, sensory, and warm; never inflated or medicinal
- Existing assets: Script wordmark, earthy brown/clay/sage palette, product photography, static HTML catalogue, and prior UI board
- Competitors or territories to avoid: Any direct imitation of competitor layouts, copy, identity, or distinctive photography

## Technical and scale context
- Current stack: Static HTML using Tailwind browser CDN, Font Awesome, and AOS
- Future target stack: Semantic HTML, compiled Tailwind CSS, modular JavaScript, Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Storage and Edge Functions), and Razorpay
- Browser/device requirements: Mobile-first responsive experience, current evergreen browsers
- Themes/locales/brands: English-first and single-brand initially; architecture should not prevent later localization
- Performance requirements: Product imagery must be optimized; core shopping routes should remain fast on mobile networks
- Governance: `design-tokens.json` will be the visual source of truth
- Security boundary: Razorpay order creation and signature/webhook verification must run in trusted Supabase Edge Functions; service-role and payment secrets must never be shipped to the browser
- Local learning-resources root: `E:\WeGroween\Resources`
- Project design-system root: `E:\WeGroween\GitHub Clone\WeGroween\design-system`
- Confidentiality and cross-project reuse: Project-private; no promotion without explicit approval

## Required deliverables
- Brand Identity Blueprint
- Three creative territories, three complete palette approaches, and two typography combinations
- Design-system documentation and machine-readable tokens
- Interactive design-system artifact
- Component and pattern specifications for future household commerce and restaurant-supply experiences
- Accessibility validation and versioned delivery snapshot

## Research questions
1. Which trust and provenance patterns make premium fresh-produce commerce credible to households without feeling clinical?
2. How should household shopping and restaurant supply coexist without creating a confusing navigation or value proposition?
3. Which catalogue, freshness, availability, delivery, substitution, and repeat-order patterns are essential for perishable goods?
4. Which visual territory can express premium authenticity while remaining distinct from generic beige-and-sage organic brands?
5. Which component contracts and governance rules will let future storefront and admin implementation remain coherent and accessible?

## Exclusions
- Medical or nutritional claims without substantiation
- A multi-vendor marketplace in the first release
- Cross-project publication of project-specific research or assets
- Copying competitor identity, layout, wording, or protected media

## Assumptions accepted for research
- Initial market: India
- Primary language: English
- Primary customer: Premium household shopper
- Secondary customer: Restaurant or hospitality buyer
- Online checkout is the primary order route; WhatsApp remains a support option
- Exact payment, fulfilment geography, delivery rules, tax configuration, and production hosting remain future implementation inputs

## Success criteria
- The brand feels premium and authentic without relying on generic luxury or eco conventions
- Future household flows are clearly supported by reusable, responsive component specifications
- Restaurant-supply and operations contexts are represented without overtaking the household-first identity
- The system is accessible, maintainable, and governed by reusable tokens and documented decisions
- The design system can be evaluated independently of a working application

research.legacy_synthesis:
# WeGroween Research Synthesis

Date: 2026-10-02  
Status: sufficient for creative-territory and architecture decisions  
Knowledge class: DERIVED

## Executive finding

The strongest opportunity is not “another organic shop.” WeGroween can own a more specific position: a premium, harvest-aware food brand that makes unusual freshness, cultivation, and seasonal variety easy for households while giving professional kitchens a credible supply path.

Premium should be demonstrated through specificity: what is growing, where and how it was cultivated, when it was harvested, how it tastes, how to use it, when it can arrive, and what remedy exists when reality changes. This is more defensible than luxury adjectives or a beige-and-sage surface treatment.

## Current-state findings

### Worth preserving
- Warm earth-derived base colors.
- Product-led photography and simple category structure.
- “Rooted in science / grown for flavor” as an early signal of cultivation knowledge.
- Directness and compact catalogue scope.

### Must change
- The script logo loses clarity at small sizes and needs a robust wordmark/lockup strategy.
- Declared typefaces are not loaded; typography is therefore uncontrolled.
- Pale/transparent text and decorative gradients require measured contrast.
- Rounded glassy bento cards feel generic and do not establish provenance or premium craft.
- The cart, mobile menu, links, and product actions are placeholders.
- Product architecture covers only mushrooms, microgreens, and combos.
- There is no serviceability, inventory, checkout, account, database, authentication, payment, or admin layer.
- Repeated page-local styles will drift and must be replaced with semantic tokens.

## Market and user findings

1. **Trust is operational.** Stronger Indian references explain source verification, delivery limits, cut-offs, refunds, and certifications before purchase.
2. **Freshness needs states.** Harvest dates, next availability, delivery windows, storage guidance, and notify-me behavior convert biological variability into useful expectations.
3. **Repeat shopping deserves first-class UX.** Buy-again, saved baskets, and eventually controlled subscriptions reduce routine effort.
4. **Perishables complicate checkout.** Serviceability, slots, stock risk, and substitutions should not appear only after a shopper has invested time.
5. **Restaurant buyers need a distinct operating mode.** Reorder speed, availability, GST-ready information, delivery status, account support, and saved lists matter more than lifestyle storytelling.
6. **Breadth needs editorial curation.** Seasonality, uses, varieties, recipes, growers, and cultivation stories prevent a broad catalogue from feeling like a commodity grid.

## Visual-system implications

- Avoid a monochrome eco-green identity and avoid default beige wellness minimalism.
- Let produce generate seasonal accents within a stable brand framework.
- Use one authoritative editorial type voice plus a highly readable UI companion.
- Prefer crisp borders, deliberate spacing, tactile paper/mineral surfaces, and controlled radii over glassmorphism.
- Commission or create original botanical marks if used; local stock-pattern files have uncertain licenses and some visible watermarks.
- Photography should show texture, scale, hands, cultivation, harvest, and finished-food context—not only isolated catalogue cutouts.

## Required experience patterns

- Early pincode/serviceability check.
- Explicit `Growing`, `Harvesting`, `Ready`, `Limited`, and `Resting` availability states with plain explanations.
- Product-card attributes appropriate to each category: pack size, harvest/dispatch timing, taste, growing method, and storage life.
- Delivery promise carried from catalogue through checkout.
- Global substitution preference plus item-level exceptions where substitutions apply.
- Buy-again and saved lists for households; rapid reorder and GST/account data for restaurants.
- Admin validation for product claims, FSSAI details, price, inventory, availability, shelf-life or best-use fields, imagery, and delivery eligibility.

## Accessibility and quality bar

- WCAG 2.2 AA target.
- Semantic native controls, visible focus, keyboard-complete flows, 44px preferred touch targets, reduced-motion support, and no color-only statuses.
- Cart, inventory, payment, and order updates must expose accessible status messages.
- Required contrast combinations will be measured before any palette becomes canonical.

## Compliance implications

The application must support qualified launch review for FSSAI, consumer-protection, tax/invoicing, privacy, refunds, delivery, and payment terms. Official FSSAI material requires food-commerce compliance and alignment between online claims and physical labels; current guidance also emphasizes valid license display and safe fulfilment. Compliance conclusions remain subject to professional legal and accounting review.

## Architecture evidence

- Next.js App Router supports server-rendered storefront routes, server-side mutations, and route handlers, but its official guidance requires authentication and authorization checks inside every server mutation and endpoint.
- Supabase can provide Postgres, authentication, and row-level authorization, but every exposed table requires deliberate grants, policies, and tests.
- Medusa provides product, order, customer, inventory, reservation, pricing, fulfilment, and admin foundations; it reduces commerce reinvention but adds a separate service and customization model.
- Razorpay is an appropriate India-oriented payment candidate, but production integration requires merchant credentials, signature verification, server-side order creation, idempotent webhooks, and reconciliation.

## Evidence gaps to carry forward

- Final service city/region, delivery radius, slot rules, and fulfilment capacity.
- Registered business name, FSSAI status, GST status, invoice rules, and policies.
- Exact product catalogue, pack sizes, pricing, stock cadence, shelf life, and claims.
- Restaurant pricing, credit terms, minimum quantities, and approval process.
- Production hosting, email/SMS/WhatsApp providers, Supabase project, Razorpay merchant account, and domain.

These gaps do not block creative-direction work or an application scaffold. They do block a compliant production launch and final operational configuration.

imagery.thesis: Cultivation and ingredient detail support quiet premium confidence; product color remains truthful
imagery.warmth: Natural neutral to gently warm; preserve believable daylight and food whites
imagery.tint: Avoid green casts and artificial palette tints
imagery.saturation: Restrained to moderate; no exaggerated green or fake freshness
imagery.exposure: Keep highlight texture and shadow detail; avoid luminous fake dew or crushed substrate
imagery.contrast: Readable food texture without harsh global contrast; overlays need their own contrast check
imagery.lighting: Soft directional daylight-like light; no clinical glare or stage-lit spectacle
imagery.texture: Preserve actual skin, leaf, mushroom, substrate and packing texture; restrained retouching
imagery.depth: Subject-led separation; keep cultivation context legible where it acts as evidence
imagery.composition: Macro food detail, scale, hands, growing beds, harvest and finished-food context; quiet backgrounds around conversion copy
imagery.crop: Product 4:3; square packshot allowed; hero/editorial 4:5 or 5:4. Preserve current R3 media geometry
imagery.negative_space: Reserve focal-safe regions for overlays; do not move copy over busy texture
imagery.background: Natural low-distraction mineral/paper/kitchen/growing contexts; separate packshot consistency from documentary evidence
imagery.palette_compatibility: C2 frames cool greens naturally; C1 blackberry remains restrained; C3 must not make food look like beauty/wine. Never grade merchandise to fit a palette.
archetype_rules: Catalogue: consistent angle/scale/padding for comparable food, no price or unit hidden
Food: appetite through credible texture and clean handling
B2B: show process evidence and labelled quantities; no invented chef testimonials
imagery.people: Hands and cultivators may explain process; obtain consent/model/property rights; avoid staged stereotypes or implied endorsements
imagery.generated_imagery: No new generated images are requested. Generated scenes may not be cultivation/provenance evidence; any future production needs separate authorization and human artifact review.
imagery.accessibility: Meaningful alt text identifies variety/context; decorative media uses empty alt; overlays require readable contrast; responsive crops preserve focal subject
imagery.performance: Use existing WebP where appropriate; define responsive crops and dimensions; optimize without food-color or texture loss; measure later
imagery.rights: R3 project-image prototype use authorized on 2026-10-03; ownership/public/production rights unverified. Exclude visible-watermark candidates. Fonts have bundled OFL.

button.anatomy: label, optional I1 icon, loading indicator

input.responsive: Full available width with labels/helper visible
input.content: Placeholder is example only; errors explain recovery

input.review_status: Specification only; rendered state/stress checks pending

card.purpose: Compare food with variety, pack, price, timing and next action
card.variants: product, category, editorial, selected/featured with semantic reason
card.responsive: Shared row geometry; stack predictably; no meaningful clipping at zoom
card.content: Shortest/longest/missing optional content and 35% expansion; preserve price/unit/action
card.accessibility: No nested conflicting links; selection and unavailability have text; focus visible
card.review_status: Specification only; rendered state/stress checks pending

badge.purpose: Communicate compact named category or availability state
badge.anatomy: text, optional I1 glyph, optional named remove button
badge.variants: neutral, brand, success, warning, error, information
badge.responsive: Remain readable at 200% zoom; wrap where needed
badge.content: Ready now, Harvest Friday, Limited, Resting; no color-only state
badge.accessibility: Text carries meaning; removable chip action is separately named

sections.title: A short path, explained before checkout.

legacy_content.text: 04 - From harvest to home A short path, explained before checkout. Delivery information is part of the shopping experience, not a policy discovered after payment. 1 Check your area Confirm the next delivery window before choosing perishable produce. 2 Choose what is ready See harvest status, pack size and timing on the product itself. 3 We pack with context Storage and use notes help the product arrive with fewer unknowns. 4 Receive your harvest Track the delivery and know whom to contact if something is wrong. Designed around local freshness Service areas, order cut-offs and delivery days should remain explicit and editable as operations grow. Read delivery guidance ->
